key_insight: Zero-point electron–phonon coupling dramatically reshapes the predicted shift-current spectrum of monolayer MoS2 despite barely changing its band dispersion.
engineering_relevance: Strain and temperature could provide tuning knobs for nonlinear photocurrents in optoelectronic and photovoltaic devices.
method: Include electronic-state renormalization from quantum virtual-phonon coupling
Evaluate shift-current responses to strain and temperature
evidence_signal: Calculations predict emergent low-energy peaks, redshifted higher-energy features, sharp tuning under 1.0% strain, and enhancement with increasing temperature.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational results, not experimental validation or demonstrated solar-cell efficiency gains.
paper_title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
